title: Ancient humans used fire way earlier than we thought!
summary:
Did you know that humans have been using fire for a super long time? A new discovery in South Africa shows that our ancient relatives, called Homo erectus, used fire as long as 1.8 million years ago. That's way earlier than anyone thought before!

The evidence comes from a place called Wonderwerk Cave. Scientists found burnt animal bones there. These bones were probably left by owls that lived in the cave. Owls cough up little balls of fur and bone after they eat. When scientists looked at these bones under a special blue light, the burnt ones glowed brighter. That's how they knew fire had been there.

Before this, the oldest known fire use was about 1 million years ago, also from the same cave. But this new find is from a deeper layer of dirt, so it's much older.

Now, the scientists don't think Homo erectus actually started the fires. They probably just picked up flames from wildfires and brought them into the cave. They used the fire for light and warmth, not for cooking.

But they didn't have fire all year round. Wildfires only happen in hot seasons. So fire wasn't always available. Still, it's amazing to think that humans have been using fire for almost 2 million years!

This discovery helps us understand how our ancestors lived and survived. Fire is a big deal for humans, and now we know we've been using it for a really, really long time.
why_it_matters: Fire keeps us warm and cooks our food, so learning when people first used it helps us understand one of the biggest steps in human history.
